evidence.observation: `ResourceLoaderReloadOptions.resolveProjectTrust`, the explicit trusted-decision hook on the reload options. The optional callback receives the bootstrap `LoadExtensionsResult` (loaded while the project is forced untrusted) and asynchronously returns whether the project is trusted. This is the only opt-in seam through which a project extension can become eligible during the same reload.

`DefaultResourceLoader.loadProjectTrustExtensions`, the bootstrap pass. It calls `settingsManager.setProjectTrusted(false)` then `reload()` before loading the current extension set, so project-local extensions and packages are deliberately excluded while user/global and temporary CLI extensions still load. Its return value is the pre-trust set handed to `resolveProjectTrust`.

`DefaultResourceLoader.reload`. The trust gate. When `options.resolveProjectTrust` is supplied, `reload` first awaits `loadProjectTrustExtensions()` (untrusted bootstrap), passes that result to the explicit decision callback, then applies `settingsManager.setProjectTrusted(projectTrusted)` before the final package/extension resolution. Without this branch no untrusted bootstrap pass occurs and project extensions are resolved under the current trust state.

`DefaultResourceLoader.loadFinalExtensionSet`. Builds the final extension set with the resolved trust state. It indexes the bootstrap extensions by resolved path (`preloadedByPath`), loads only the `remainingPaths` (which can now include the previously filtered project extension), reuses the bootstrap `runtime`, and returns the ordered final list. A project extension therefore appears in `getExtensions()` only when the explicit decision was trusted.

claims.claim: During bootstrap the loader is forced into the untrusted trust state and returns an extension set that excludes the project extension while still including user/global extensions, so a fresh project extension is unavailable at that point.

Availability of the project extension is decided by the explicit `resolveProjectTrust` callback: `reload` runs the untrusted bootstrap pass, feeds its `extensionsResult` to the callback, and applies the returned boolean via `setProjectTrusted` before resolving the final set.

`loadFinalExtensionSet` reuses the bootstrap-loaded extensions and loads the remaining paths (including the project extension) under the applied trust state, so the project extension becomes available in the final result only after, and only because of, a trusted decision.

conclusion: A fresh project extension is unavailable during bootstrap and becomes available only after an explicit trusted decision. `DefaultResourceLoader.reload` calls `loadProjectTrustExtensions()`, which forces `setProjectTrusted(false)` so the bootstrap result contains user/global and CLI extensions but not the project extension. The explicit `resolveProjectTrust` callback receives that pre-trust result; `reload` applies its boolean return via `setProjectTrusted` and only then does `loadFinalExtensionSet` load the remaining project path. The demo's trusted scenario shows the project extension in the final set, and the untrusted scenario shows it remains absent.
